summary: Dependency-confusion PoC with install-time and import-time OAST DNS beacons
details: rcp-ndcg 9999.0.0 is a dependency-confusion proof-of-concept squatting an unclaimed name referenced by cohere-ai's rcp-ndcg README, using an implausibly high version (9999.0.0) to win resolution against any internal package of that name. setup.py performs socket.getaddrinfo() to rcp-ndcg-build.<token>.oast.site at sdist build time, and src/rcp_ndcg/__init__.py performs a sibling getaddrinfo() to rcp-ndcg-import.<token>.oast.site on import. Both subdomains resolve through Interactsh (oast.site), a third-party out-of-band DNS collector controlled by the publisher, so each install and each import leaks the event and the resolver's IP to that collector. The package ships no legitimate functionality; its only observable behavior is the beacon. The sdist builds on all listed default platforms, so a plain `pip install rcp-ndcg` triggers the install-time callback, and any later `import rcp_ndcg` triggers the import-time callback.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
